body:
Nothing is popping on the arbitrage side today: the scanner returned zero opportunities across both venues. That's a legitimate quiet-day result, not a gap in coverage — it's checked live order books on both Kalshi and Polymarket gold contracts and found no mispricing large enough to clear fees after accounting for fill depth.

Prices tell a coherent story of a market that pulled back slightly from August's highs. Spot gold was quoted around $4,419.61 on Sept 7 by JM Bullion, a bit off the roughly $4,465 print Forbes had a few days earlier. Gold spot price today slides to $4,420 after a strong August jobs report revives Fed rate-hike bets, though physical demand holds firm, according to USAGold. That level lines up with what the order books show: Kalshi's Sept 30 above $4,410.99 settle contract sits almost at a coin flip (bid 0.44 / ask 0.48), which is exactly what you'd expect when the strike sits right on top of the current spot price.

One thing worth explaining rather than flagging as an edge: Polymarket's weekly touch $4,400 low contract trades at 0.94–0.95, near-certain, while a same-strike Kalshi settle contract for month-end sits closer to a coin flip. These aren't comparable products. Polymarket's contracts pay out if spot merely touches a level anytime during the week's trading, while Kalshi's settle contracts pay only on the official price at one specific moment (5:00 PM EDT, Sept 30, or year-end). A volatile week can easily touch both a $4,400 low and a $4,450 high without ending anywhere near either at settlement — which is what the pattern here suggests, not a free-money mismatch. Several of the far-out-of-the-money strikes also show zero 24h volume, a reminder that thin books can make quoted prices look more interesting than they are.
headline: No arbitrage today: gold pricing across Kalshi and Polymarket is internally consistent
